title: Node Auto Repair now drains through disruption budgets and PDBs

detection.reason: only applies with the NodeRepair feature gate on, and the controller's env VALUES are not collected (names only) — the hint names the controller, the command reads the gate

quote: **Breaking:** Node Auto Repair (alpha, `NodeRepair` feature gate) is now a voluntary disruption method. Instead of forcefully terminating an unhealthy node, Karpenter pre-spins a replacement, respects NodePool Disruption Budgets under the new `Unhealthy` reason, and drains the node while respecting PDBs. The drain is bounded by a per-condition termination grace period; see Monitored Node Conditions. Use the new `karpenter.sh/do-not-repair: "true"` node annotation to opt individual nodes out of repair; see Annotations. With the default budget (`nodes: 10%`), Karpenter repairs at most 10% of a NodePool's nodes at a time. The CRD adds `Unhealthy` to the budget `reasons` enum, so upgrade your CRDs alongside the controller. See CRD Upgrades above.
remediation: Only matters if the `NodeRepair` feature gate is on. From 1.15 an unhealthy node is no longer terminated outright: Karpenter launches a replacement first, takes a NodePool disruption budget under the new `Unhealthy` reason (default `nodes: 10%`, so at most 10% of a pool is repaired at once), and drains the node respecting PodDisruptionBudgets, bounded by the repair policy's drain time (10 minutes, 5 for GPU XID faults, or the NodeClaim's `terminationGracePeriod` if shorter). A budget with no `reasons` now covers `Unhealthy` too, so a NodePool frozen with `nodes: "0"` (or inside a zero-budget schedule window) gets NO repair at all — list `reasons` on that budget if repair must keep working. Repair also stops for a NodePool with more than 20% of its nodes unhealthy, and `karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt` on a node does not block it. Upgrade the CRDs with the controller — the `Unhealthy` budget reason is new in the CRD. Annotate nodes `karpenter.sh/do-not-repair: "true"` to opt them out. On clusters with 1000+ nodes where repair now slows disruption, `settings.legacyNodeRepair` (`LEGACY_NODE_REPAIR=true`) brings back the old forceful health controller.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("karpenter/controller")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \([.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(FEATURE_GATES|AWS_FEATURE_GATES|LEGACY_NODE_REPAIR)$")) | "\(.name)=\(.value)"] | join(" "))"'; kubectl get nodepools -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | "\(.metadata.name) budgets=\(.spec.disruption.budgets // [] | tojson)"'  # NodeRepair=true in FEATURE_GATES (env only; a --feature-gates arg is not read) turns repair into a budgeted drain; a pool printed with a budget of nodes 0 and no reasons gets no repair at all
coversNotes: Legacy health controller: Clusters with 1000+ nodes that enable node repair may see disruption slow down …
The default repair policies bound the drain at 10 minutes, or 5 minutes for GPU XID faults.

title: Bottlerocket NVIDIA nodes on Kubernetes 1.37 need a 6Gi root volume

detection.reason: bites only node classes that set blockDeviceMappings themselves AND launch Bottlerocket NVIDIA AMIs on 1.37+; blockDeviceMappings is not collected. The hint names node classes whose amiFamily or amiSelectorTerms alias is Bottlerocket

quote: The default Bottlerocket root volume (`/dev/xvda`) size is now `6Gi` (previously `4Gi`). Bottlerocket v1.66.0+ `aws-k8s-1.37-nvidia` AMIs have a 6 GiB root snapshot, and launches with a smaller root volume fail with `InvalidBlockDeviceMapping`. This only applies to EC2NodeClasses that do not set `blockDeviceMappings`. If you set `blockDeviceMappings` yourself and use Bottlerocket NVIDIA AMIs on Kubernetes 1.37+, set the `/dev/xvda` `volumeSize` to at least `6Gi`. This default change does not drift existing nodes, and new nodes pick up the larger volume as they launch.
remediation: Nothing to do for node classes that leave `blockDeviceMappings` unset: the default root volume of every new Bottlerocket node grows from 4Gi to 6Gi (2Gi more EBS per node), without drifting existing ones. If a Bottlerocket node class sets `blockDeviceMappings` itself and launches `aws-k8s-1.37-nvidia` AMIs, raise the `/dev/xvda` `volumeSize` to at least `6Gi` — a smaller root volume fails the launch with `InvalidBlockDeviceMapping`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ec2nodeclasses -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | select((.spec.amiFamily // "" | test("(?i)bottlerocket")) or ([.spec.amiSelectorTerms[]?.alias // ""] | any(test("(?i)^bottlerocket")))) | "\(.metadata.name) xvda=\([.spec.blockDeviceMappings[]? | select(.deviceName == "/dev/xvda") | .ebs.volumeSize] | join(","))"'  # a Bottlerocket class printed with an xvda size below 6Gi fails NVIDIA 1.37 launches

title: Pods steer consolidation with the deprecated pod-deletion-cost annotation
quote: **Deprecation:** Karpenter now reads the `karpenter.sh/disruption-cost` annotation to decide which pods are cheaper to disrupt during consolidation. Using `controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost` to steer consolidation is deprecated. If you set `controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost` on your pods to influence Karpenter consolidation, set `karpenter.sh/disruption-cost` to the same value instead. Karpenter still falls back to `controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost` when `karpenter.sh/disruption-cost` is absent, but only while the `PodDeletionCostManagement` feature gate is disabled, and the fallback is planned to be removed in a future release.
remediation: If these pods set `controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost` to influence which nodes Karpenter consolidates, add `karpenter.sh/disruption-cost` with the same value. Karpenter 1.15 reads the new annotation first and falls back to the old one only while the `PodDeletionCostManagement` feature gate is off; the fallback is planned for removal, and turning that gate on makes Karpenter overwrite or remove the old annotation on ReplicaSet pods. Pods that set it only for ReplicaSet scale-down need nothing.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost"] != null) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) cost=\(.metadata.annotations["controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost"]) karpenter=\(.metadata.annotations["karpenter.sh/disruption-cost"] // "-")"'  # karpenter=- on a row means the pod steers consolidation only through the deprecated annotation

title: EC2NodeClasses with kubelet settings their AMI family cannot apply launch no nodes

detection.reason: reads the resolved AMI family (amiFamily, else the amiSelectorTerms alias), the spec.kubelet key names and the clusterDNS count the agent projects from 0.4.157; an EC2NodeClass synced by an older agent is not judged

quote: Any other field set on those families is rejected rather than silently dropped: the `ValidationSucceeded` status condition is set to `False` with reason `UnsupportedKubeletConfiguration`, and no nodes launch from the NodeClass until the unsupported fields are removed. Two field-level restrictions are enforced the same way, for the same reason:
remediation: Before upgrading, check every EC2NodeClass whose AMI family is not `AL2023` or `Custom` (`AL2`, `Bottlerocket`, `Windows2019`/`2022`/`2025`, including classes that pick the family through an `amiSelectorTerms` alias). On `Bottlerocket`, remove `spec.kubelet.podsPerCore` — Bottlerocket never applied it, so running nodes do not change. Reduce `spec.kubelet.clusterDNS` to one entry — these families only ever passed the first one to the kubelet. Karpenter 1.15 sets `ValidationSucceeded=False` (`UnsupportedKubeletConfiguration`) on a class that still has either and launches no nodes from it until it is fixed. From 1.15 `spec.kubelet` accepts any KubeletConfiguration field, but on these families only the 12 mapped fields are allowed; any other field added later is rejected the same way.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ec2nodeclasses -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | (.spec.amiFamily // ([.spec.amiSelectorTerms[]?.alias // empty] | first // "" | split("@")[0])) as $f | select($f != "" and ($f | test("(?i)^(al2023|custom)$") | not)) | select(((.spec.kubelet.podsPerCore != null) and ($f | test("(?i)^bottlerocket$"))) or (.spec.kubelet.clusterDNS[1]? != null)) | "\(.metadata.name) family=\($f) podsPerCore=\(.spec.kubelet.podsPerCore // "-") clusterDNS=\(.spec.kubelet.clusterDNS // [] | length)"'  # a printed class launches no nodes on Karpenter 1.15 until the field is fixed
coversNotes: Only the `AL2023` AMI family bootstraps nodes with a full kubelet configuration document, so it is the only …
`podsPerCore` is not applied by the `Bottlerocket` family.
`clusterDNS` accepts only one entry on these non-AL2023 families, not a list.
The `Custom` AMI family is exempt from these checks.
